basis: Neurodevelopmental impairment with brain abnormalities; strabismus affects 5/9 patients. Feeding difficulty and hypotonia do not establish separate organ damage.
Acquired disorder of mineral metabolism; no specific organ damage is inherent across this group.
Gonadotropin deficiency defines the disease; olfactory bulb hypoplasia/aplasia and impaired smell occur in 3/3 annotated patients.
Malignancy of the urachus, a urinary bladder remnant.
Neoplasm occupying the brain, meninges or spinal cord; additional organs depend on the individual tumor.
Emergomyces fungal infection; disseminated series show skin lesions in about 95% and pulmonary involvement in over 70%; frequencies vary by species and host.
Demyelinating peripheral neuropathy; distal muscle atrophy and pes cavus occur in 100% of reported patients; hearing impairment is frequent (30-79%).
Histiocytic neoplasm with characteristic bone lesions; endocrine dysfunction 80-99%, cardiovascular infiltration about 50-70%; renal involvement ≥30% omitted at cap.
Peters anomaly subtype affecting corneal and anterior segment development.
Malignant germ cell tumor arising in the pericardium.
Benign neoplasm of cerebral blood vessels; associated brain injury is not established by this concept.
Necrosis of renal papillae, potentially impairing concentration and obstructing urinary drainage.
Myoclonic epilepsy syndrome; no additional organ involvement is established.
Destructive periodontitis 88% and characteristic skin fragility/pretibial plaques; joint hypermobility 46% and scoliosis 33% support musculoskeletal involvement.
Mitochondrial neurodegeneration; visual impairment 100%, optic atrophy 83%, hearing loss 79%; muscle atrophy 70% and cardiomyopathy 36% omitted at cap.
Fibromuscular dysplasia directly affects the coronary arterial walls.
B-lineage acute leukemia involving hematopoietic cells and marrow; no additional organ damage is established as common.
Brainstem/cerebellar malformation with developmental impairment; eye movements and breathing abnormalities are neurologic. Retinal dystrophy 10%, renal/hepatic disease 5%.
Malignant smooth-muscle neoplasm placed in the CNS by its supplied parent; smooth-muscle histology alone does not establish skeletal-muscle involvement.
Clonal myeloid proliferation in bone marrow; thrombosis and extramedullary organ damage are not uniformly common across this umbrella.
Developmental and intellectual impairment commonly accompany partial chromosome 16 duplications; other organ malformations vary with the duplicated segment.
Autoimmune blistering disease of skin; mucosal damage varies substantially among subtypes and is not established as common across the umbrella.
Disorder of cutaneous sweating affecting palms and soles.
Inherited nephritis with progressive renal dysfunction; hearing loss depends on the Alport subtype and is not established at ≥30% across this heterogeneous group.
Isolated inherited dilated cardiomyopathy; ventricular dysfunction and heart failure occur in 2/2 annotated patients.
